claim: Goldman Sachs Research stated in April 2023 that only about 4% of global creators are deemed professionals, meaning they earn more than $100,000 a year, and expected that share to stay steady as the ecosystem expands.
stance_target: The claim that the share of creators earning a professional income is a low single-digit percentage and structurally stable
scope_conditions: Global; Goldman Sachs Research article dated 19 April 2023 summarizing Eric Sheridan's team report; note that Goldman's own March 2025 report defines professional/amateur by self-identified full-time versus part-time status rather than by any income threshold, so the $100,000 attribution is inconsistent across Goldman's own publications
quoted_support: Only about 4% of global creators are deemed professionals, meaning they pull in more than $100,000 a year. Goldman Sachs Research expects their share of the creator universe to stay steady even as the overall ecosystem expands.
region: Global; $100,000 is a US income benchmark

claim: Goldman Sachs projected the creator economy total addressable market roughly doubling from $250 billion in 2023 to $480 billion by 2027, growth it explicitly benchmarks to global digital advertising spend rather than to creator earnings.
stance_target: The use of creator economy market-size projections as evidence about creator incomes
scope_conditions: Global; total addressable market, not realized revenue; growth rate tied to digital ad spend forecasts; TAM includes platform and brand spending, most of which does not reach creators
quoted_support: the total addressable market of the creator economy could roughly double in size over the next five years to $480 billion by 2027 from $250 billion today ... That growth is roughly in line with the team's estimates for growth in global digital advertising spend over that period.

claim: Goldman Sachs asserted that brand deals are the main creator revenue source at about 70%, attributing the figure only to unnamed 'survey data' with no sample size, fielding date, or sampling frame disclosed.
stance_target: The evidentiary basis of the claim that brand deals dominate creator income
scope_conditions: Global; Goldman Sachs April 2023 article; the underlying survey is unnamed but the figure is close to the NeoReach/Influencer Marketing Hub 77% figure from a self-selected 2021 survey of an influencer-agency roster, and directly contradicts Linktree's finding that 70% of creators earn under 10% of income from brand deals
quoted_support: Brand deals are the main source of revenue at about 70%, according to survey data.
numbers: ~70% of creator revenue from brand deals

claim: Goldman Sachs expected the 50 million global creator population to grow at a 10-20% compound annual rate over five years from 2023, a range it narrowed to 10% in its March 2025 update.
stance_target: The stability of institutional creator population forecasts
scope_conditions: Global; 2023 forecast of 10-20% CAGR versus 2025 forecast of ~10% CAGR to 107 million by 2030
quoted_support: Goldman Sachs Research expects the 50 million global creators to grow at a 10-20% compound annual growth rate during the next five years.
